facts.fact: The Bhakti movement first developed in South India (7th–12th centuries).
Saguna Bhakti is devotion to a God with form and attributes.
Kabir and Guru Nanak belong to the Nirguna stream.
The Alvars were 12 Vaishnava saints.
The Nayanars were 63 Shaiva saints.
The Nalayira Divya Prabandham has 4000 Tamil verses.
The Tevaram is the collection of Shaiva hymns.
Shankara — Advaita; Ramanuja — Vishishtadvaita; Madhva — Dvaita.
Shankara founded mathas at Sringeri, Dwarka, Puri and Badrinath.
Ramananda preached Ram Bhakti in vernaculars and took disciples of all castes.
Kabir's compositions are in the Bijak and the Adi Granth.
Guru Nanak introduced Langar.
Guru Nanak's precepts were Nam Japna, Kirat Karna and Vand Chhakna.
Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas.
Surdas wrote the Sursagar.
Vallabhacharya founded the Pushtimarga.
Dnyaneshwar wrote the Dnyaneshwari, a Marathi commentary on the Gita.
The Varkari sect worships Vithoba at Pandharpur.
Tukaram composed Abhangas.
Namdev's hymns are in the Guru Granth Sahib.
Basavanna founded Lingayatism with Ishtalinga worship.
Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti founded the Chishti order in India at Ajmer.
A khanqah was the hospice where Sufis lived and taught.
A silsilah is a Sufi order or lineage.
Sama is a musical gathering (qawwali).
Fanaa is self-annihilation in God.
The Suhrawardi order was brought to Multan by Bahauddin Zakariya and kept close ties with the state.
The Naqshbandi order followed strict Islamic law and opposed sama.
Under the Qadiri order Miyan Mir enrolled Dara Shikoh.
Amir Khusrau pioneered sabaq-i-hindi and used Persian metres in Hindawi.
Annamacharya composed Telugu sankirtanas to Venkateswara of Tirumala-Tirupati.
Bammera Potana wrote the Andhra Mahabhagavatamu.
Vemana wrote aphoristic Satakam verses critical of caste and ritual.
Bhadrachala Ramadasu built the Bhadrachalam temple and was jailed by the Golconda ruler.
Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri are the Carnatic Trinity.
Tyagaraja's five celebrated compositions are the Pancharatna kritis.
Bhakti and Sufism spread devotional literature in regional languages.
Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a woman Nayanar.
Andal was the woman Alvar.
Mirabai was a Rajput princess devoted to Krishna.
Lingayat Vachanas were debated at the Anubhava Mantapa.
A dargah is a saint's tomb-shrine; the urs is the death-anniversary festival.
The pir (murshid) is the Sufi master and the murid the disciple.
The Khalsa was not created by Guru Nanak.
Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar are the three Nayanars whose hymns form the Tevaram.
Manikkavachakar wrote the Tiruvasagam.
Sekkilar wrote the Periya Puranam, the lives of the 63 Nayanars, at the court of the Chola Kulottunga II.
Nathamuni (10th c.) compiled the Nalayira Divya Prabandham.
Nammalvar is regarded as the greatest Alvar (Tiruvaymoli).
Periyalvar was the foster-father of Andal; Andal's Tiruppavai is sung in the month of Margazhi.
The Alvars stressed prapatti — total surrender to Vishnu.
Adi Shankaracharya was born at Kaladi in Kerala.
Sringeri matha is linked with the Yajur Veda, Puri with the Rig Veda, Dwarka with the Sama Veda and Badrinath with the Atharva Veda.
Ramanuja's magnum opus is the Sri Bhashya, a commentary on the Brahma Sutras.
Ramanuja headed the Srirangam temple community.
Madhvacharya founded the Krishna matha at Udupi.
Madhva taught a fivefold difference (panchabheda) among God, souls and matter.
Nimbarka taught Dvaitadvaita (dualistic non-dualism) with Radha-Krishna worship.
Basavanna was a minister of the Kalachuri king Bijjala at Kalyana.
Allama Prabhu was a 12th-century Vachana mystic, one of the Lingayat trinity.
Akka Mahadevi was the woman Vachana poet of the Lingayat trinity.
Madara Chennaiah is regarded as the father of Vachana poetry.
Lingayats follow Shatsthala (six stages) and Panchacharas (five codes of conduct).
The Nathpanthi tradition was founded by Matsyendranath and developed by Gorakhnath.
The eighteen Siddhars of Tamil Nadu are linked with Siddha medicine.
Dnyaneshwar also wrote the Amrutanubhav, a treatise on non-duality, and belonged to the Nath tradition.
Nivruttinath, elder brother of Dnyaneshwar, initiated him into the Nath tradition.
Eknath wrote the Bhavarth Ramayana and the Rukmini Swayamwar; his guru was Janardan Swami.
Tukaram lived at Dehu near Pune.
Chokhamela, of the Mahar caste, wrote Abhangas protesting untouchability.
Soyarabai, Chokhamela's wife, called herself 'Chokha's Mahari'.
Bahina Bai (1628–1700) was a woman Varkari poet, devotee of Tukaram.
Gora Kumbhar was a potter-saint devoted to Vitthala.
Narhari Sonar was a goldsmith-saint of Pandharpur.
Kanhopatra, a courtesan's daughter, became a Varkari saint.
Bhanudas (1448–1513) revived the Vithoba temple at Pandharpur.
Samarth Ramdas founded the Samarth Sampradaya and wrote the Dasbodh and Manache Shlok.
Kabir was brought up by Neema and Niru, a Muslim weaver couple of Varanasi.
Kabir's cryptic, paradoxical sayings are called ulatbansi.
Ravidas (Raidas) was a leather-worker saint whose poems are in the Guru Granth Sahib.
Tradition makes Ravidas the guru of Mirabai.
Tulsidas is credited with the Sankatmochan temple at Varanasi and with starting the Ramleela.
Vallabhacharya taught Shuddhadvaita (pure non-dualism).
Sankardev (1449–1568) founded Ekasarana Dharma (neo-Vaishnavism) in Assam.
Sankardev set up namghars (prayer halls) and sattras (monasteries) and composed Borgeet.
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu of Bengal spread Gaudiya Vaishnavism through sankirtan and spent his later life at Puri.
Dadu Dayal of Rajasthan founded the Dadu Panth.
The source PDF dates Ramananda to 1486–1533, but standard books place him in the 14th–15th century, before Kabir.
Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki, successor of Muinuddin Chishti, settled at Delhi.
Baba Farid (Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar) wrote in Punjabi; his verses are in the Adi Granth.
Nizamuddin Auliya, the Chishti saint of Delhi, saw seven sultans and kept away from the court.
Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Delhi ('Lamp of Delhi') succeeded Nizamuddin Auliya.
Shaikh Hamiduddin Nagauri translated Persian mystic verse into Hindawi.
Shaikh Salim Chishti of Sikri blessed Akbar with a son (Salim).
The Suhrawardi order was founded by Shihabuddin Suhrawardi (Baghdad); Bahauddin Zakariya brought it to Multan.
The Firdausi order, a Suhrawardi branch in Bihar, is linked with Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri.
The Rishi order of Kashmir was founded by Shaikh Nuruddin Wali (Nund Rishi).
Wahdat-ul-Wujud (unity of being) was developed by Ibn-i-Arabi.
Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi countered it with Wahdat-ul-Shuhud (unity of appearance).
The yogic text Amrita Kunda was translated into Arabic and Persian.
Zikr is the repeated recitation of God's name.
Tauba is repentance.
A khalifa is a disciple appointed as successor or deputy of a pir.
Ziyarat is pilgrimage to the tomb of a Sufi saint.
Hal is a mystical state of ecstasy.
Biddat means an innovation not in line with orthodox Islam.
Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib, now in Pakistan) and had his enlightenment at Sultanpur (1496).
Guru Angad (Bhai Lehna) standardised the Gurmukhi script.
Guru Amardas organised the community into 22 manjis and opposed sati and purdah.
Guru Ramdas founded Ramdaspur (Amritsar) and composed the Anand Karaj marriage hymn.
Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth (1604) and completed the Harmandir Sahib; he was the first Sikh martyr.
Guru Hargobind introduced Miri-Piri and built the Akal Takht.
Guru Har Rai sheltered Dara Shikoh.
Guru Har Krishan, the child Guru, died of smallpox at Delhi; Gurdwara Bangla Sahib honours him.
Gurdwara Sis Ganj in Chandni Chowk marks where Guru Tegh Bahadur was beheaded.
Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699 at Anandpur Sahib.
The five Ks are kesh, kangha, kara, kachera and kirpan.
Guru Gobind Singh died at Nanded (Hazur Sahib) in 1708.
The Guru Granth Sahib was completed at Damdama Sahib (Talwandi Sabo).
Annamacharya was born at Tallapaka (Annamayya district, AP).
Annamacharya's sankirtanas are of two kinds — adhyatma (spiritual) and sringara (romantic).
Kshetrayya of Movva (Krishna district) composed Telugu padams to Muvva Gopala.
Tarigonda Vengamamba was an 18th-century woman poet-devotee of Venkateswara.
Narayana Tirtha wrote the Sanskrit dance-drama Krishna Leela Tarangini.
Siddhendra Yogi shaped the Kuchipudi dance-drama and wrote Bhama Kalapam.
Tyagaraja lived at Tiruvaiyaru on the Kaveri, where his aradhana is held.
Vemana's verses end with the refrain 'Viswadabhirama Vinura Vema'.
